title: Kunneth formula, one proper factor, $\kunZn$-coefficients
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed
field and let $n\ge1$ be an integer invertible in $k$. Let $X$
be a proper scheme over
$k$ and let $Y$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$. For
$E\in D(X_{\Et},\kunZn)$ and $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\kunZn)$ the Kunneth
map

$$
\kappa_{E,K}:
\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\kunZn}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)
\longrightarrow
\RGamma\bigl((X\times_kY)_{\Et},
\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism. (*Source:* Stacks Project, Tag
[0F14](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F14), part (2).)

proof.text: Put $S=\Spec(k)$, $f=a_X:X\to S$, $g=a_Y:Y\to S$, $W=X\times_kY$, $p=\operatorname{pr}_1$, $q=\operatorname{pr}_2$, and $c=fp=gq$. Set $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, $F=p^{-1}E$, $T=F\otimes^L_\Lambda q^{-1}K$, $A=R\Gamma(X_{\Et},E)$, and $B=R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},K)$. Proper stability [lem-kun-proper-stability] makes $q$ proper. The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0,k$; $\Spec(k)$ has the single affine chart and is quasi-compact. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to the given finite-type $g$ makes $Y$ Noetherian, in particular quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. Then [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes $Y$ quasi-separated. These facts check the geometric hypotheses of the projection formulas used below; separatedness of $Y$ is not assumed.

source.place: Tag 0F14, label lemma-kunneth-one-proper (2); qcqs hypotheses from Tags 01T6, label lemma-finite-type-noetherian, morphisms.tex, and 01OY, label lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated, properties.tex

proof.text: We spell out the point-topos convention. By [lem-kun-0ezp] every small etale object $U\to S$ is a disjoint union $\coprod_{i\in I}S$. The component covering and sheaf gluing give $H(U)=\prod_{i\in I}H(S)$ for any sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules $H$, naturally under morphisms of such objects. The constant sheaf [def-kun-constant-sheaf] with value $M$ has the same formula $\underline M(U)=\prod_{i\in I}M$. Thus evaluation at $S$ and the constant-sheaf functor are inverse additive exact equivalences between module sheaves on $S_{\Et}$ and $\Lambda$-modules. They identify tensor products by their universal property on each component and preserve direct sums, kernels and cokernels, since the inverse equivalences identify their universal properties. Applied termwise they therefore identify cohomology and the direct-sum total tensor complexes of [def-kun-derived-tensor]: degree $m$ evaluates to $\bigoplus_{i+j=m}C^i(S)\otimes_\Lambda D^j(S)$ with differential $d_C\otimes1+(-1)^i1\otimes d_D$. Thus they preserve acyclicity and quasi-isomorphisms. They therefore induce a tensor-compatible equivalence $D(S_{\Et},\Lambda)=D(\Lambda)$ on the entire unbounded categories: a tensor with an acyclic complex is acyclic on one side exactly when its image is, so K-flat complexes and derived tensors correspond as well. The sign symmetry corresponds to the ordinary sign symmetry. For any scheme $V\to S$ with map $a$, evaluation of $Ra_*H$ is $R\Gamma(V_{\Et},H)$: on a K-injective resolution $I$ both are represented by $\Gamma(S,a_*I)=\Gamma(V,I)$, and evaluation is exact, as in [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]. In particular $Rf_*E$ corresponds to $A$ and $Rg_*K$ to $B$.

source.place: Tag 0F14, label lemma-kunneth-one-proper, proper-base-change identification; point-site decomposition: Tag 0EZP, label lemma-Rf-star-zero-normal-with-alg-closed-function-field, specialized to Spec(k); component-cover sheaf axiom

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-0f0c] to the cartesian square $(p,q,f,g)$ and $E\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Its hypotheses hold because $f$ is proper and $n\ge1$; the theorem permits arbitrary $g$ and unbounded complexes. It gives the canonical exchange isomorphism $g^{-1}Rf_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*p^{-1}E=Rq_*F$. By step 2 $Rf_*E$ is the constant complex with value $A$ on $S$. Pullback of constants [lem-kun-pullback-constant] identifies its inverse image on $Y$ with $\underline A$. Denote the resulting exchange isomorphism by $e:\underline A\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*F$. We retain this canonical exchange, rather than choosing an arbitrary isomorphism of these objects.

source.place: Tag 0F14, label lemma-kunneth-one-proper, proof (2) via proof (1), proper-base-change identification; Tag 0F0C, label lemma-proper-base-change-mod-n

proof.text: The ring $\Lambda$ is torsion since $n\Lambda=0$. Apply [lem-kun-0f0g] to the proper map $q$, the arbitrary object $F\in D(W_{\Et},\Lambda)$, and $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$. It gives the canonical projection-formula isomorphism $t:Rq_*F\otimes^L_\Lambda K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*T$. This application imposes no boundedness or constructibility condition on either complex. We will use $t^{-1}$ followed by $e^{-1}\otimes1_K$.

source.place: Tag 0F14, label lemma-kunneth-one-proper, proof (2) via first display of proof (1); Tag 0F0G, label lemma-projection-formula-proper-mod-n

proof.text: Use small representatives of the sites in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to the small etale topoi with constant ring $\Lambda$ and the maps $q:W\to Y$, $g:Y\to S$. This is the canonical comparison $Rc_*T\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rq_*T$ in unbounded module categories. More explicitly, choose a K-injective representative $I$ of $T$ and a K-injective resolution $j:q_*I\to J$. The cited statement says $g_*j$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Exact evaluation on $S$ from step 2 makes $\Gamma(S,g_*j)=\Gamma(Y,j)$ a quasi-isomorphism from $\Gamma(W,I)$ to $\Gamma(Y,J)$. The defining resolution recipe [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] identifies these as the representatives of $R\Gamma(W,T)$ and $R\Gamma(Y,Rq_*T)$. Hence we obtain the canonical Leray isomorphism $\ell:R\Gamma(W,T)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(Y,Rq_*T)$. This is the canonical unbounded composition comparison used by the compatibility lemma below; using it avoids additional finite-cohomological-dimension hypotheses on $q$.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, label lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, supplying the Leray comparison in etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0F14, label lemma-kunneth-one-proper, proof (2)

proof.text:
Since $Y$ is finite type over the separably closed $k$, clause (2) of [lem-kun-0f10] gives $\operatorname{cd}(Y)<\infty$. Together with the qcqs property proved in step 1 and the torsion ring $\Lambda$, this verifies all hypotheses of [lem-kun-0f12], with its scheme $X:=Y$, object $E:=K$, and constant complex $K:=A\in D(\Lambda)$. Thus its canonical map $r:B\otimes^L_\Lambda A\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(Y,K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline A)$ is an isomorphism. Let $\sigma$ denote the symmetry from [lem-kun-tensor-sym], on $Y_{\Et}$ and on $S_{\Et}$ (the latter gives symmetry on $D(\Lambda)$ via step 2). Consequently every arrow in the composite
$$\theta=\sigma_{B,A}\circ r^{-1}\circ R\Gamma(Y,\sigma_{\underline A,K})\circ R\Gamma(Y,e^{-1}\otimes1_K)\circ R\Gamma(Y,t^{-1})\circ\ell:
R\Gamma(W,T)\longrightarrow A\otimes^L_\Lambda B$$
is an isomorphism, so $\theta$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0F14, label lemma-kunneth-one-proper, proof (2), last sentence; Tags 0F10, label lemma-finite-cd, and 0F12, label lemma-pull-out-constant-mod-n

proof.text: It remains to identify the specified morphism. For the square $(p,q,f,g)$ and ring $\Lambda$, [def-kun-kunneth-map] defines it as $Rc_*(\alpha_{E,K})\circ\eta_{c}$: the transpose $\alpha_{E,K}$ is the inverse tensor comparison, followed by the two canonical inverse-image composition maps, followed by $p^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,E}\otimes^L_\Lambda q^{-1}\varepsilon_{g,K}$. Under the exact point equivalence in step 2 this is precisely the displayed global-sections map $\kappa_{E,K}:A\otimes^L_\Lambda B\to R\Gamma(W,T)$. Clause (b) of [lem-kun-kunneth-map-agrees] applies: $k$ is separably closed, $f$ is proper, $Y$ is finite type over $k$, $n\ge1$ is invertible in $k$, and the inputs are in the full unbounded $\Lambda$-module derived categories. Its $e,t,\ell,r$ are exactly the canonical exchange, proper projection-formula map, composition comparison, and constant-complex projection map retained in steps 3--6, in the same orientations. Its compatibility equation therefore gives $\theta\circ\kappa_{E,K}=1_{A\otimes^L_\Lambda B}$. Since step 6 has independently shown $\theta$ invertible, multiplying this equation by $\theta^{-1}$ yields $\kappa_{E,K}=\theta^{-1}$. Thus the canonical Kunneth map is an isomorphism.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed
field and let $n\ge1$ be an integer invertible in $k$. Let $X$
be a proper scheme over
$k$ and let $Y$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$. For
$E\in D(X_{\Et},\kunZn)$ and $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\kunZn)$ the Kunneth
map

$$
\kappa_{E,K}:
\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\kunZn}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)
\longrightarrow
\RGamma\bigl((X\times_kY)_{\Et},
\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
The proof is exactly parallel to the proof of
[lem-kun-0f14a]: by [lem-kun-proper-stability] the morphism
$\operatorname{pr}_2$ is proper, and the projection formula of
[lem-kun-0f0g] (with the torsion ring
$\Lambda=\kunZn$) gives

$$
R\operatorname{pr}_{2,*}
\bigl(\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr)
\cong
R\operatorname{pr}_{2,*}\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}K .
$$

Proper base change in the unbounded form of
[lem-kun-0f0c] yields
$R\operatorname{pr}_{2,*}\pr_1^{-1}E\cong \underline{\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)}$, the pullback of a constant object
being constant ([lem-kun-pullback-constant],
[lem-kun-tensor-unit]). Since $Y$ is of finite type over the
separably closed field $k$, [lem-kun-cd-sep-closed-point] and
[lem-kun-0f10](2) give $\kuncd(Y)<\infty$; since moreover
$\operatorname{pr}_2$ is a morphism of finite type schemes over
$k$, [lem-kun-0f10](1) gives $\kuncd(\operatorname{pr}_2)< \infty$, so [lem-kun-leray-unbdd] applies and

$$
\RGamma\bigl((X\times_kY)_{\Et},
\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr)
\cong
\RGamma\bigl(Y_{\Et},
\underline{\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)}\kunotimes{\kunZn}K\bigr) .
$$

By [lem-kun-0f12] (with the constant complex
$\underline{\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)}\in D(\kunZn)$) and
[lem-kun-tensor-sym] we get an isomorphism $\theta$ to
$\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\kunZn}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)$, and
[lem-kun-kunneth-map-agrees](b) shows
$\theta\circ\kappa_{E,K}=\mathrm{id}$. Hence $\kappa_{E,K}$ (the
Kunneth map of [def-kun-kunneth-map]) is an isomorphism.
